Net sales $109.8M, +163% YoY, vs. $90.0M consensus (EarningsWhispers). H1 2026 net sales $214.7M, +204% YoY.

growth.note: This is organic product-revenue growth (DDR4/DDR5 memory modules), distinct from the separate Oct 2026 Micron patent-licensing settlement income. Company guided Q3 2026 product revenue 'similar to Q2' on the July 30 call.

nextEarnings.note: Investing.com says Nov 3; EarningsWhispers and Digrin say Nov 5 (before open). No company press release or 8-K found confirming either. Using Nov 5 as the more-corroborated estimate (2 sources vs 1).

price.source: Webull/Finviz settlement-day coverage (carried from prior pass)

catalysts.headline: Latham & Watkins (Netlist's lead ITC counsel) announced that the October 2026 Netlist-Micron settlement/license agreement resolved the parties' dispute at the ITC as well as all other pending litigation between Netlist and Micron
catalysts.impact: Confirms the Oct 5-6 settlement closed out the DDR5 Section 337 investigation (337-TA-1472, instituted Sept 23, 2026) as between Netlist and Micron specifically; status of that investigation as to the other three respondents (Super Micro, HPE, Lenovo) not stated

catalysts.headline: NLST shares closed at $6.66, up ~18% on the day following the Micron settlement; stock up more than 970% over the trailing year, with market value described as above $2 billion
catalysts.impact: Major positive price reaction to the settlement news

catalysts.headline: Netlist and Micron agreed to a $600 million patent license and settlement, resolving pending litigation between the companies
catalysts.impact: Micron receives a 5-year license to Netlist's patent portfolio and will pay $30M per quarter for 20 quarters (Q4 2026 through Q3 2031), totaling $600M; settles and mutually releases pending legal proceedings between the companies

catalysts.headline: Netlist announced a NEW, separate ITC Section 337 complaint accusing Micron's HBM3E/HBM4/HBM4E products (patents 12,308,087 and 12,646,537) of infringement, also naming Nvidia, Broadcom and Google as respondents over use of the accused HBM chips in AI computing systems; this is distinct from the already-settled DDR5 RDIMM/MRDIMM case (337-TA-1472)
catalysts.impact: Opens a new, unresolved litigation front against Micron (and three additional large tech companies) that is NOT covered by the October Micron settlement, which only released 'pending' litigation as of its Oct 5 signing; could be a fresh overhang/catalyst independent of the settled DDR5 matter
catalysts.note: Filing/announcement date conflicts across sources: company press release datelined Sept 29, 2026; one outlet reports the complaint was first filed confidentially on Sept 25, 2026; another source states ITC institution as Investigation No. 337-TA-1523 on Sept 23, 2026 (likely a conflation with the unrelated Aug 11, 2026 DDR5 complaint, which other sources instead identify as 337-TA-1523) — institution number/date not independently resolved this session

catalysts.headline: US ITC instituted a Section 337 investigation into Micron, Supermicro, HPE, and Lenovo over alleged infringement of Netlist DDR5 patents (the underlying complaint was filed by Netlist in August 2026)
catalysts.impact: Opens a second litigation/exclusion-order track against four large respondents; it is unclear from available sources whether the October 2026 Micron settlement resolves Micron's portion of this ITC matter specifically
catalysts.source: Date carried over from pre-existing record; general background corroborated via search summary referencing Netlist's ITC filing, exact institution date not independently re-confirmed this session

catalysts.headline: US ITC votes to institute a Section 337 investigation into Micron, Super Micro Computer, HPE and Lenovo over alleged infringement of four Netlist DDR5 RDIMM/MRDIMM patents, based on Netlist's complaint
catalysts.impact: stock jumped intraday (reported variously as ~12.7% to ~14.5%)

catalysts.headline: Roth Capital analyst Suji Desilva raised Netlist price target to $15 from $10, maintaining a Buy rating, citing the ITC complaint against Micron/Super Micro/HPE/Lenovo and the precedent of Netlist's Samsung settlement/SK Hynix license
Netlist announced a five-year strategic alliance with Samsung Electronics
catalysts.impact: cited by Roth Capital as supporting rationale for its subsequent price-target increase

catalysts.headline: Netlist reported Q2 2026 results: net sales $109.8M (+163% YoY) vs. $90.0M consensus; net income $1.4M vs. a $6.1M net loss in Q2 2025; H1 2026 net sales $214.7M (+204% YoY); management guided Q3 2026 product revenue to be similar to Q2
catalysts.impact: First organic-growth earnings beat alongside the ongoing patent-litigation narrative; shares reportedly fell premarket despite the beat per one secondary headline ('Plunges 16% Pre-Market Despite Q2 Revenue Beat, Stuck at Break-Even EPS')

conflicts: New ITC HBM complaint (Micron/Nvidia/Broadcom/Google): announcement/filing date given variously as 2026-09-25 (Reuters, confidential filing), 2026-09-27, and 2026-09-29 (company press release); the ITC docket number is also disputed — one source ties it to 337-TA-1523 (which a different source instead assigns to the earlier, unrelated Aug 11 2026 DDR5 complaint against Micron/Supermicro/HPE/Lenovo) — not reconciled this session.

Next earnings date: this session found a THIRD estimate — EarningsWhispers' beta page lists Oct 29, 2026 — in addition to the on-file conflict between Investing.com (Nov 3) and EarningsWhispers/Digrin's non-beta pages (Nov 5). Still no company 8-K or press release confirming any date.
notes: Primary new finding this session: Netlist has an active, unsettled ITC complaint (filed ~late Sept 2026) against Micron, Nvidia, Broadcom and Google over HBM patents, separate from the DDR5 dispute that the Oct 5-6 Micron settlement and the Oct 21 Latham announcement closed out. This HBM matter does not appear to be resolved by the Micron settlement and is worth tracking as a live catalyst. No new confirmed price or share-count data found this session (same stale/conflicting figures as prior passes).
